prompt:
Research what the Home Assistant project has officially published about the number of active installations (its opt-in analytics). Cite the page and quote the numbers.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
I looked at the official Home Assistant analytics site and the project's own blog/docs. Here's what I found that speaks directly to the number of active installations and how the project itself frames those numbers.

A quick note on interpretation: the "active installations" figure is the count of installations that have *opted in* to analytics — Home Assistant is private by design and doesn't phone home, so this is a floor, not a total. The project has said so explicitly (see the 2021 blog post). Also note that the analytics pages are live dashboards, so the figures I quote are what those pages currently display (I captured them on 2026-10-07); they will keep changing.

SOURCE: https://analytics.home-assistant.io/ | QUOTE: "695,026 Active Home Assistant Installations" | CLAIM: Home Assistant's official analytics dashboard currently reports 695,026 active installations — that is, installations that have opted in to share analytics data.

SOURCE: https://analytics.home-assistant.io/ | QUOTE: "Analytics in Home Assistant are opt-in and do not reflect the entire Home Assistant userbase. We estimate that less than a fourth of all Home Assistant users opt in." | CLAIM: The project itself states the active-installations count is only the opt-in subset, and estimates fewer than 25% of actual users are included in it.

SOURCE: https://analytics.home-assistant.io/statistics/ | QUOTE: "496,813 of 637,194 (77.97%) installations have chosen to share usage statistics" | CLAIM: Of the installations reporting analytics at the time captured, 637,194 shared basic analytics and 496,813 (77.97% of those) went further and shared detailed usage statistics.

SOURCE: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/analytics | QUOTE: "The Analytics system was introduced in Home Assistant 2021.4, and it's used by 76.5% of the active installations." | CLAIM: The analytics integration documentation reports that 76.5% of active installations have the analytics integration enabled.

SOURCE: https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2021/11/12/100k-analytics/ | QUOTE: "Our estimate is that there are 4-5x more installations than people that opt-in to analytics." | CLAIM: In 2021 the project officially estimated the true number of installations was 4–5 times the opt-in analytics count, reinforcing that the dashboard number is a fraction of the real total.

SOURCE: https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2025/04/16/state-of-the-open-home-recap/ | QUOTE: "One big announcement Franck made was that this year we went from 1 million to over 2 million active installations in 2024!" | CLAIM: In the 2025 State of the Open Home, the project publicly stated Home Assistant passed 2 million active installations during 2024 — an internally-reported total that goes well beyond the opt-in analytics figure.

A caveat worth stating plainly: the 2-million figure from the 2025 blog post and the ~695k figure from the analytics dashboard are measuring different things. The dashboard counts only opt-in analytics participants, while the 2-million figure is the project's broader estimate of actual active installations. The project has not (as far as I could find) published a methodology for how it arrives at totals like "2 million," so I can't source how that number is derived.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: The methodology Home Assistant uses to calculate its total active installation count (e.g., the "2 million" figure) beyond the opt-in analytics data — the project states the number but does not publish how it was estimated.
